primitives.verbatim_quote: - Bayes' Rule in high dimensions: $p(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}) = \frac{p(\mathbf{y} \mid \theta) p(\theta)}{\int p(\mathbf{y} \mid \theta) p(\theta) d\theta}$.

primitives.name: Conditional Gaussian Distribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Conditional Gaussian identities: $$\boldsymbol{\mu}_{1|2} = \boldsymbol{\mu}_1 + \mathbf{\Sigma}_{12} \mathbf{\Sigma}_{22}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_2 - \boldsymbol{\mu}_2)$$ $$\mathbf{\Sigma}_{1|2} = \mathbf{\Sigma}_{11} - \mathbf{\Sigma}_{12} \mathbf{\Sigma}_{22}^{-1} \mathbf{\Sigma}_{21}$$ - **GSE Transfer:** Live conditional probability updates during 175-snap simulation when observing in-game yardage and score states.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\boldsymbol{\\mu}_1, \\boldsymbol{\\mu}_2': 'mean vectors, dimensionless', '\\mathbf{\\Sigma}_{11}, \\mathbf{\\Sigma}_{22}, \\mathbf{\\Sigma}_{12}': 'covariance matrices, variance units', '\\mathbf{x}_2': 'observed variables, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Joint distribution is multivariate normal; conditioning on known subset is valid.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When covariance matrix is singular or rank-deficient, inversion fails.

primitives.name: Variational Inference with ELBO
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Chapter 8 & 9: Variational Inference & Approximations - Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO): $$\ln p(\mathbf{y}) \ge \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}[\ln p(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{z})] - \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}[\ln q(\mathbf{z})] = \text{ELBO}(q)$$ - Mean-field factorization: $q(\mathbf{z}) = \prod_{j=1}^m q_j(\mathbf{z}_j)$.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{y}': 'data, vector-valued', '\\mathbf{z}': 'latent variables, vector-valued', 'q(\\mathbf{z})': 'variational distribution, probability density', 'p(\\mathbf{y}, \\mathbf{z})': 'joint distribution, probability density'}
primitives.assumptions: Latent variables are conditionally independent under mean-field assumption.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When true posterior is not in variational family, ELBO underestimates log-evidence.

The core mathematical structure of Bayesian inference underpins all three primitives. The first, Bayes’ Rule, defines how beliefs evolve with new data—this is foundational for GSI’s prior construction and player rating systems. The second, conditional Gaussian identities, enables precise modeling of interdependencies in multivariate spaces such as player kinematics and team dynamics. These are essential for GSE’s real-time simulations where in-game observations update internal state estimates. The third, variational inference, allows scalable approximate posteriors that bypass computationally expensive MCMC methods—critical for GSE’s simultaneous evaluation of 77 player prop lines. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop system: prior → likelihood → posterior → action, enabling both static modeling and dynamic reasoning.
